Delhi Metro Makes Extensive Arrangements to Manage Additional Crowd amid Ongoing DTC Bus Strike

The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) today put in place extensive arrangements to manage the anticipated surge in passenger footfall on its network due to the ongoing Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) bus strike.

To ease pressure on the system, DMRC has increased 20 train trips across its network. A total of eight additional trains were operated today as per requirement. 

These measures are aimed at accommodating a higher number of passengers, particularly during peak hours, and ensuring smoother travel for commuters.

The same enhanced arrangements will continue tomorrow, 17 September 2026. Eight extra trains will be inducted and operated between 08:00 hrs and 20:00 hrs, as per operational requirements.

DMRC remains committed to providing reliable and efficient services and requests passengers to plan their journeys accordingly.

text:
DELHI METRO SARTHI APP CROSSES 1-CRORE DOWNLOADS, OFFERS SEAMLESS ACCESS TO MULTIPLE SERVICES

The Delhi Metro Sarthi app has emerged as the Delhi Metro network’s premier ticketing solution provider with over one crore downloads and close to 20 lakh views in the Delhi NCR in a month. The app is opened 8.2 lakh times every week (weekdays) thus, establishing itself as a reliable mode of ticketing for Metro commuters. 

The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) is making daily commuting simpler and more convenient through this app, which brings a range of  transport and other services together on a single, easy-to-use digital platform.

Sarthi is designed to provide commuters with a seamless digital experience, reducing the need to switch between multiple platforms while planning and undertaking their journeys.

The app integrates various transport services, including DTC buses, train bookings through IRCTC, interstate bus bookings, NCRTC’s Namo Bharat and NMRC’s Noida Metro. This integration allows commuters to access different modes of public transport through a common platform.

The app also provides several everyday commuter facilities such as Metro maps, first and last Metro timings, parking information, station facilities, EV charging stations and battery-swapping stations along with route guidance.

Beyond mobility, Sarthi also offers services such as mobile recharge, medicine ordering, FASTag recharge and other utility payments. The app also provides a virtual Metro card facility.

With these features brought together in one place, the Sarthi App is emerging as a convenient digital mobility companion for commuters, providing easier access to transport information, ticketing and other essential services.

The initiative is part of DMRC’s efforts towards creating a connected, digital-first and commuter-centric mobility ecosystem, while encouraging greater use of integrated public transport.

During the winter months, the national capital faces significant challenges pertaining to pollution. During this period especially, the people of Delhi NCR shall be encouraged to use the Metro more often and use this app for their ticketing requirements.

author: RaviRaj91HQ
author_bio: Notes that explain: facts, critique, analysis
text:
Naveen Malik, a contractual Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) driver was suspended for posting the demands of DTC bus drivers on social media.

Naveen claims that ten more drivers have been suspended by private vendor companies for participating in the strike.

In a video, he states that:

DTC doesn't allow drivers to do more than 1 shift a day. 

However, Naveen claims that his vendor company issued him three identification cards, all three has his photo on the card but the details on the card are of some other person. 

When concerned authorities from DTC do the routine checks, he was been instructed by his vendor company to show one ID card in the morning and the other for the next shift he is assigned.

Naveen further claimed that, doing multiple shifts a day is one of the major reasons of bus accidents in Delhi, as drivers do not get enough time to sleep.

He also revealed that drivers are pressured to do "OK duty". A term used by vendor operator companies of DTC to describe on time entry and exit from bus-stops and depots, as more rounds a drivers makes, more the money is paid to the vendors companies. 

Hence, compelling the drivers to drive faster, in order to qualify as "OK duty".

Naveen is just one such case, a big bus driver strike is going on right now in Delhi for about 7 days now.

Yet much of the attention has focused on the disruption to commuters, rather than the working conditions of drivers behind the strike.

The protesting drivers point out that while permanent Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) drivers earn regular monthly salaries (around ₹40,000 to ₹48,000), contract drivers are paid a flat daily wage of just ₹862 per day. 

Many drivers report that their pay has stagnated for over a decade.

Drivers also state that they are only given basic routine training but receive no training in disaster management or handling emergencies.

Their claims identify regular overtime shifts and poor training as a major result of accidents of DTC bus drivers.

Protesting driver are reportedly being arrested for vandalism and other offences from the various protest sites across Delhi.

It's almost like the Delhi Government doesn't care about these drivers.

Contractual DTC drivers are demanding a wage increase, alongside medical insurance, social security benefits, paid leave, government action on illegal overtime shifts forced on drivers by private companies and removal of financial penalties and liability imposed on drivers for minor bus damages or breakdowns.

The government says most of the demands have been accepted, while the drivers' union says the key issues remain unresolved. 

The wage question has now been referred for consultation with the Labour Department.

These drivers are not just asking for higher wages. They are asking for basic security, reasonable working hours and safer conditions on the roads.

If their allegations are true, the problem is bigger than one suspended driver or one ongoing strike. It is about a system in which the people operating Delhi’s public transport may be carrying the greatest risks while having the least security.

Because Delhi’s buses cannot be safe if the people driving them are not.

author: kkstau
author_bio: Occasional columnist and regular calumnist | Storyteller at Teen Taal #TTStaff | History-Religion-Politics | Hi-Ur-En | BR-JH-UP
text:
Jailbreak in Reverse
The government machinery has granted Abhijeet Dipke his first wish. He couldn't begin Jail Bharo on Gandhi Jayanti, had the permission been granted.

His primary demand has been: arrest me. The Centre let a minister go to deny him. The announced demand for this protest remains that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar pack up.

It began, as most official things do, with a no. Mumbai Police told the Cockroach Janta Party it could not protest at Shivaji Park on October 2, citing among other things that the ground is a silence zone. That's the first condition for a Jail Bharo Andolan fulfilled.

What is a Jail Bharo? You voluntarily fill the jails, that is what the phrase sounds like. But a jail has one small entrance on a large door and it is locked and heavily guarded. Nobody has ever been seen walking in on their own, mujhe andar jaane ka hai, please jaane do. Nope. Never. So a little history.

The most successful Jail Bharo in independent India was run by Indira Gandhi, and not one volunteered then. On the night of 25 June 1975, the state did the bharo-ing itself. By the Shah Commission’s count, over 1,10,000 people were arrested. JP, Vajpayee, Advani, all picked up at midnight, in their pyjamas. Nobody had to court arrest. Arrest courted them. Because if you have been in the business of courting you know it's a no, 99% of the times. 

The jails were housefull even before Indiraji's order. Indian jails are always overflowing beyond capacity. Reportedly, on Gandhi Jayanti that year, Gandhians were picked up from Rajghat itself. Gandhi arrested Gandhians from Gandhi Samadhi because Gandhi knew where a true Gandhian would be found on Gandhi Jayanti. 

The OG Gandhi did it the other way round. Mahatma Gandhi went to jail on purpose, 2,089 days in India and 249 in South Africa. At home, it was often not a jail jail. In 1942 his address was the Aga Khan Palace in Pune, which is not a five-star listing, but close enough for the times. A man who had mastered the art of going to jail found that the British, being good hosts when it suited them, made sure the jail was mostly a guesthouse. The Raj was the most reliable logistics partner an andolan could ask for. Break the salt law and it obliged with a lathi and a lock-up. Everyone wanted the same outcome, which is rare in Indian politics.

Which brings us back to Shivaji Park, and the confusion. Jail Bharo is supposed to be the special protest, the big one. But look at what it involves. You gather where you have no permission to gather, and the police come and take you away. Now tell me which protest in this country does not end like that. Ask Yogendra Yadav, who is often bundled into a bus, driven around, and released by dinner. The Constitution says the police must produce an arrested person before a magistrate within 24 hours, or let him go. Police don't want to get into legal lafda, they know how painful law can be, so most volunteers are merely detained, and the jail in Jail Bharo in Delhi is, in practice, a DTC bus on Dilli Darshan. Every protest in India is a Jail Bharo. Nobody calls it Jail Bharo. And it never ends up in a jail. 

Picture the scene. October 2, Shivaji Park. Same Cockroaches, one megaphone, the pigeons losing interest, and constables who have to decide whether they fulfill the demand. If the police arrest them, the aandolan succeeds but since they are taken to the Mumbai equivalent of Delhi's Chhatrasal stadium, the aandolan both fails and succeeds. It's not a jail. If the police don’t, and let everyone sit there sloganeering, the aandolan both fails and succeeds. The Mumbai Police holds both the koschan paper and the kunji. The protesters pass either way. Schrodinger's Jail Bharo Andolan.

In a country where a normal protest is already a jail bharo, the Cockroaches have found a way.

Zor se bolo, Jail Bharo.  
Saare bolo, Jail Bharo.  
Shaam ko bolo, Bail Bharo.

But shaam ko on a Gandhi Jayanti Friday? Monday ko aana

Chaired a comprehensive review meeting today on strengthening women’s safety measures across Delhi, particularly within the DTC bus network, along with @CPDelhi and the Secretary (Transport).

It was decided that female police personnel will be deployed inside DTC Ladies Special Buses, which will be operated by women staff on identified vulnerable routes with high female ridership. In addition, Women Home Guard Marshals will also be deployed to assist them and further enhance commuter safety and confidence.

A key decision was also taken to directly integrate Panic Button alerts in buses with the 112 PCR emergency response system of @DelhiPolice, enabling faster and more effective response mechanisms.

Further, Delhi Police will soon establish dedicated all-women Police Stations across every district of Delhi to exclusively handle cases and complaints relating to crimes against women and children with greater sensitivity and efficiency.

Delhi remains firmly committed to ensuring dignity, safety, and empowerment for every woman. Simultaneously, focused efforts are underway to significantly increase female representation across concerned departments to strengthen the vision of a Safe, Surakshit and #ViksitDilli.
